name: Tapo P125M Mini Smart Wi-Fi Plug (Matter)

radios.note: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi (IEEE 802.11b/g/n). TP-Link lists Bluetooth for setup only.

matter.note: TP-Link calls it Matter-certified and the US datasheet lists Matter among its certifications. We did not find a CSA listing that names the P125M model number.

apple_home.note: TP-Link lists Apple Home. The plug has no HomeKit (HAP) mode, so this works through Matter and needs an Apple home hub.

google_home.note: Added in the Google Home app by scanning the Matter code. Linking through Tapo Actions may also work, but we found no source that confirms it for this model.

alexa.note: TP-Link's Alexa guide says Matter-enabled Tapo devices connect to Alexa directly, not through the Tapo skill. Needs an Echo that works as a Matter controller.

smartthings.note: TP-Link lists Samsung SmartThings. We could not confirm a direct Tapo cloud integration, so we record it as Matter.

home_assistant.note: Home Assistant's TP-Link Smart Home integration lists the P125M among supported Tapo plugs. It can also be added through the Matter integration.

hubRequired.note: No hub is needed with the Tapo app. Third-party ecosystems need their own Matter controller.

localControl.note: TP-Link says Matter devices on your home network can still be controlled from the Tapo app or another Matter app without internet.

energyMonitoring.note: The US product page and datasheet don't list energy monitoring, and TP-Link forum staff say the P125M lacks it. The Italian datasheet lists it, so regional versions may differ. No official US statement either way.

maxLoadWatts.note: 15 A / 1800 W maximum for resistive loads at 100–125 V.

summary: The Tapo P125M is TP-Link's compact US Wi-Fi smart plug with Matter. It is rated 15 A / 1800 W and uses 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, with Bluetooth used only for setup. TP-Link lists support for Apple Home, Alexa, Google Assistant and SmartThings, and you can set it up by scanning the Matter code.
caveats: Apple Home works only through Matter, which needs an Apple home hub (HomePod or Apple TV).
The Matter pairing window lasts 15 minutes, and the controller must be on the same local network.
